attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his July 2026 post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition matches the sentence. Only the first half is testable: a present-tense observation that capacity massively outpaces demand. The second half is a conditional mechanism that is close to true by definition. 'Causal' fits only the unscored half, so the scored claim is an observation.

contract.note: The language is firm and names no measure. Reading demand as leasing, booking and paying for capacity is the ordinary meaning, and it covers the near-term pipeline. His deeper point, demand backed by sustainable revenue, is flagged and not scored. H1 2026 is a fair window for 'coming online'.

evidence.note: CBRE market research on H1 2026, published Aug 2026. Vacancy held at 1.4%, over 80% of capacity under construction was preleased, and asking rents rose. This is the opposite of a massive oversupply. It covers all data centers in eight North American markets, not AI-only capacity.

Secondary report of Microsoft's April–June 2026 earnings call. The CFO said demand surpasses supply and new capacity is monetized immediately. This is a company statement about itself, which the contract accepts as a source.
Independent SemiAnalysis tracker, March 2026. Capacity coming online through Aug–Sep 2026 was already booked, and one-year H100 rental prices rose sharply.

reviews.rationale: On the fair plain reading, H1 2026 data show tight supply: 1.4% vacancy, over 80% preleasing, rising rents and GPU rental prices, and a major provider saying demand exceeds supply. The one counter-signal, a report of softer spot H200 prices, could not be dated. The data do not test whether demand is funded sustainably, which is the speaker's likely deeper point. The conditional half is not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion of fact and his own inference. Only the quoted contract phrase comes from CoreWeave.

semantics.note: The proposition foregrounds the hedged inference ('suggesting' unsold capacity). It drops facts he asserted firmly: the $6.3B CoreWeave backstop, the residual-capacity obligation through April 2032, and spending of $6B or more a year. The contract restores these as the tested elements.

contract.note: Testing the factual premises he stated firmly is fair. Leaving the hedged 'anti-demand' and 'suggesting unsold' inference unscored follows policy. The yearly schedule is listed among the tested elements but is not part of the support condition.

evidence.note: Secondary summary of NVIDIA's 10-Q for the quarter ended 26 April 2026. It reports $30B in multi-year cloud service agreement commitments.
Contemporary May 2026 report confirming $30B, up from $27B. NVIDIA ties the agreements to R&D. That counters his reading but not the figure.
Quotes CoreWeave's SEC disclosure: NVIDIA is obligated to buy residual unsold capacity through April 13, 2032.
Confirms the $6.3B order dated September 9, 2025, running to April 13, 2032.
From NVIDIA's July 2026 10-Q, filed after the post. It describes how the commitments shrink as third parties use the capacity. This bears on the unscored inference only.

reviews.rationale: Both parts of the support condition are met: about $30B in multi-year cloud commitments as of April 2026, and a $6.3B CoreWeave order obliging NVIDIA to buy residual unsold capacity through April 2032. The '$6B or more a year through 2028' schedule could not be verified from a citable source, but nothing contradicts it. The hedged inference about unsold capacity is not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own thesis, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The proposition faithfully isolates the final clause; the demand parts sit elsewhere. 'Asset bubble with ruinous consequences' is an evaluative thesis with a vague, undated future element. It is not a checkable observation.

contract.note: The contract rightly finds no test, threshold or deadline for 'bubble' or 'ruinous'. Checking only that construction is debt-funded would not test the claim.

reviews.rationale: Calling an asset class a bubble with ruinous consequences sets no measure, size, affected party or deadline. It can be confirmed only after a collapse, and the post gives no criterion. The packet found no realized losses by the cutoff, but absence of losses would not settle it either. The case is untestable as stated, not broken.

attribution.note: Zitron's own statement, which he stresses is 'not hyperbole'.

semantics.note: The revision keeps his 'vast majority' wording and the full proposition. It is a firm present-tense observation.

contract.note: The 70% or more threshold is consistent with his own '70% to 90%' figure nearby. Reading 'contingent on' as revenue share plus reliance on outside funding is ordinary. 'Unsustainable' is left unscored, which is fair.

evidence.note: Barclays puts OpenAI and Anthropic at 13% of AWS exposure in 2026. This covers one provider and is measured against total AWS revenue, not AI compute revenue, so it is a different metric. The article otherwise relays the speaker's own arguments.
Bull-case counterpoint citing Microsoft's commercial backlog (RPO) and Copilot seats. It does not measure the two labs' share of AI compute revenue.
NVIDIA's August 2026 guarantee of OpenAI leases, from a filing after the post. It bears on how OpenAI's compute is financed, outside the target period.

reviews.rationale: No sector-wide measure of OpenAI and Anthropic's share of AI data center compute revenue was found. The single-provider figures (13% at AWS, 27% at Google Cloud) use total cloud revenue as the base and do not test the 'vast majority' claim. Nothing in the packet measures how far the two labs' compute payments depend on fundraising in the period.
